extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in NLP/LLM evaluation (ML/NLP community)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating freeform LLM generations by using other LLMs as judges, specifically proposing and assessing a Panel of LLM evaluators (PoLL) composed of many smaller, diverse models as an alternative to a single large judge. The paper studies cost, bias, and performance trade-offs across multiple judge settings and datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of LLMs as judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Many evaluations now rely on using LLMs themselves as judges to score the quality of outputs from other LLMs, because evaluating the correctness of freeform generations is challenging and data to probe particular model properties is hard to obtain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider automated LLM-based judging when human evaluation is infeasible or when scaling is required, but be aware this approach introduces its own costs and biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problems with a single large judge
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluations most commonly use a single large model like GPT-4 as the judge, but this method is costly, has been shown to introduce intra-model bias, and very large models are often unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying solely on a single large judge due to monetary cost and risk of biased assessments that reflect the judge-model's idiosyncrasies rather than true quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel of LLM evaluators (PoLL) as alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed approach: evaluate models using a Panel of LLM evaluators (PoLL) composed of a larger number of smaller models rather than one large judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement panels of multiple smaller models to aggregate judgments; according to the paper this can outperform single large judges while being substantially cheaper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of model families to reduce intra-model bias
rubrics_metrics.description: A PoLL composed of disjoint model families exhibits less intra-model bias due to its composition of diverse models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct panels from heterogeneous model families (different architectures/providers/sizes) to mitigate bias that stems from any single model family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number-of-models vs single-model scale trade-off
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a larger number of smaller models can outperform a single large judge and be more cost-effective (the paper reports being over seven times less expensive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize assembling sufficiently many and diverse smaller evaluators rather than defaulting to the largest available judge; evaluate cost-performance trade-offs empirically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate across multiple judge settings and datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Robust evaluation should be tested across different judge settings and multiple datasets — the paper evaluates three distinct judge settings and six datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluation experiments that span varied judge configurations and datasets to assess generality and avoid overfitting conclusions to a single setting or dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty of finding targeted evaluation data
rubrics_metrics.description: Finding data to adequately probe particular model properties is difficult, which motivates automated or alternative evaluation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When targeted data are scarce, supplement human annotation with diverse automated judges or create datasets specifically designed to probe properties of interest, while validating judges' reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge of judging correctness for freeform generations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing the correctness of freeform model outputs is intrinsically challenging, motivating the exploration of alternative judge mechanisms (e.g., panels) rather than simplistic single-judge scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use richer evaluation protocols (ensembles/panels, disagreement analysis, calibrated aggregation) for freeform NLG tasks rather than single-score judgments.
